title: Handoffs and channel claims are deleted; their open rows become work items

story.as_a: session or Mark looking for open work
story.i_want_to: find every piece of work as a work item, with no handoff posts or channel claims left beside them
story.so_that: one piece of work has one record and one done state, and the chg#77 case of four copies cannot recur

rationale: PRD section 4: channel_claims and channel_claim/channel_done/channel_release are 'deleted: claiming a work item is the story claim; open claims migrate to stories', and the handoff: key prefix, the handoff MCP tool and escalation handoffs are 'deleted with the move verb that replaces them'. chg#77 lived as an issue, a handoff, a story and an escalation with separate done states (PRD section 1). After US-52.43 to US-52.46 a handoff is a move and an ad-hoc item, so the parallel mechanism goes in this release, rows migrated, with no shim (README epic-wide rules).

acceptance_criteria.description: Loopctl.Factory.MigrateHandoffs.run/1 turns each open handoff (the newest live, unsuperseded, unquarantined channel post per handoff: key with no done claim, on any host) into a story at stage detected in its project's intake source target epic, else in an epic 'Migrated handoffs' it creates, with the body as description and a plan note holding the key, author agent, session, host and posted date; a key of EscalationHandoffs.handoff_key/3's form instead adds that note to its escalated story and creates nothing.

Each channel_claims row with done_at null and a live lease is carried to the story its ref became (or a new detected story titled by the ref): the story is claimed for the row's claimant_holder_id with the claim's lease_expires_at when that holder is live, and left unclaimed otherwise.
Every story the migration creates carries metadata migrated_from {kind, id}; a second run creates and changes nothing, and run(dry_run: true) returns the counts per project and kind without writing.

After the migration the release drops the channel_claims table and deletes ChannelClaim, ChannelClaimController, ChannelClaimSweeper and its cron, EscalationHandoffs, EscalationHandoffWorker and its cron, Escalations' close_handoffs/2, and Coordination's claim/5, done/6, release/6, claims_page/3, directed_handoffs/3, directed_handoffs_page/3 and maybe_derive_handoff_key/1; GET /api/v1/channel/handoffs and the /api/v1/channel/claims routes answer 404.

After MigrateHandoffs.run/1, a migration removes exactly what US-52.22 left for handoff: rows: it sets expires_at = LEAST(expires_at, inserted_at + the tenant's channel_message_retention_days) on every row whose key starts handoff:, then drops channel_posts_session_key_uidx, channel_posts_handoff_discovery_idx and the key column; Messages.insert/2 loses its 30-day handoff branch, a post carrying key is refused 422 keyed_slot_retired, and a body starting handoff: is stored as an ordinary channel message.

The MCP tools handoff, channel_handoffs, channel_claim, channel_release, channel_done and channel_claims are removed with mcp-server/lib/handoff.js and claim-session.js and their README rows, and a node test asserts none of the six names is declared or dispatched.

e2e/test/two_sessions_one_repo_test.exs (US-52.20) loses its channel_claim step (AC-52.20.4) and the channel-claim half of its leaves-nothing-open check (AC-52.20.8), because channel_claim no longer exists; the scenario otherwise runs unchanged and passes, and this story adds no e2e path.

CHANGELOG.md has a breaking-change entry naming every removed route and tool with its replacement (work_item_move, work_item_open, message_send, claim_story), and docs/repo-coordination-bus.md, README.md and Projects.Merge's table list no longer mention channel_claims or handoff posts.

test_cases.name: open handoffs become stories once (DataCase)
preconditions: project P with an intake source targeting epic E; project Q with none; on P a live handoff:repo#812 post, a superseded one, a done one; on Q a live handoff:q-1; an escalation handoff key for escalated story S
expected_results: counts only; one detected story in E, one in Q's new 'Migrated handoffs' epic, a plan note on S and no story for it; the rerun adds nothing

test_cases.name: live claims carry their holder (DataCase)
preconditions: live claim on handoff:repo#812 by live holder H; live claim on ref 'lane:x' by an ended holder; expired claim on 'lane:y'
expected_results: repo#812's story assigned_holder_id H, claimed_until = the claim's lease; lane:x story unclaimed; nothing for lane:y

test_cases.name: tenant isolation: a handoff migrates into its own tenant (DataCase)
preconditions: live handoffs in tenants A and B with the same key
expected_results: one story in each tenant, each under its own project

test_cases.name: removed surface (ConnCase + unit)
preconditions: an agent key that is a project member; before the drop migration, a handoff:repo#3 post 20 days old with its 30-day expires_at, in a tenant with no retention setting
steps: run the drop migration's up/0, then read the handoff:repo#3 row
expected_results: expires_at = inserted_at + 7 days (already past); then 404; 404; 201 with no key; 422 keyed_slot_retired; false

test_cases.name: the six tools are gone (node --test)
preconditions: mcp-server tool list and dispatch switch
expected_results: none declared, none dispatched; route_coverage passes

test_cases.name: e2e: the two-sessions scenario runs without channel claims
preconditions: mix e2e against loopctl.com after this release deploys

test_cases.name: docs and changelog name the replacements (doc check)
steps: grep the changelog entry for each removed tool
expected_results: no stale mention; each removed tool appears with its replacement

technical_notes: Deleted, with today's lines: lib/loopctl/coordination/channel_claim.ex (schema :95); lib/loopctl_web/controllers/channel_claim_controller.ex; lib/loopctl/workers/channel_claim_sweeper.ex and its cron (lib/loopctl/oban_config.ex:573); lib/loopctl/delivery/escalation_handoffs.ex and lib/loopctl/workers/escalation_handoff_worker.ex with its cron (oban_config.ex:790-794); Escalations' alias and close_handoffs (lib/loopctl/delivery/escalations.ex:86,473-495); Coordination claim/5 :1660, done/6 :1733, release/6 :1810, claims_page/3 :2202, claim_done_retention_days/0 :1541, max_directed_handoffs/0 :380, maybe_derive_handoff_key/1 and @handoff_anchor_regex :755-766, directed_handoffs/3 :3739, directed_handoffs_page/3 :3769 and handoff_visibility_filter :3850; routes router.ex:290,321-325; FallbackController's claim clauses (fallback_controller.ex:15,134-182); ChannelPostController's handoffs action; the handoff wording in api_spec/schemas.ex:1204,1346,1415; tier_capabilities.ex:87's text.

What releases 3 and 4 leave, and this story removes: channel_claims gained claimant_holder_id (US-52.14 AC-52.14.6), which AC-52.49.2 reads; US-52.22 left key only on handoff: rows (AC-52.22.5), channel_posts_session_key_uidx rebuilt with the predicate key LIKE 'handoff:%' (first built priv/repo/migrations/20260717020000_create_channel_posts.exs:54, rebuilt 20260718000000_harden_channel_posts_slot_and_ordering.exs:49-54), a 30-day expires_at for handoff: rows only (AC-52.22.3, Coordination.retention_days/0), and channel_posts_handoff_discovery_idx (20260719160000_add_channel_posts_handoff_discovery_idx.exs:22). key is the schema field at lib/loopctl/coordination/channel_post.ex:186. to_host, to_capability and superseded_by (channel_post.ex:184-185,200) stay: superseded_by is read beyond handoffs, and dropping the other two is not in PRD section 4's list.

MCP: declarations at mcp-server/index.js:3960 (handoff), :4117, :4207, :4232, :4250, :4314 and dispatch cases :10500-10535; lib/handoff.js and lib/claim-session.js; the escalation playbook's handoff wording (lib/escalation-playbook.js).

Migration order: one Ecto migration calls MigrateHandoffs.run/1 (rows through context functions on AdminRepo, the escalation note through release 3's notes writer, story claim through Progress.claim_story/3 with holder_id), a later one drops the table and columns; Projects.Merge's @tables and unique-key list drop channel_claims (lib/loopctl/projects/merge.ex:42,51).
New stories open their stage row at detected so release 6's intake re-check and triage take them like any reported item: nothing is left for Mark.

claude-config's handoff skill (skills/handoff/SKILL.md), bin/handoff-issue.sh and the hooks that read handoffs or claims (gate-claimed-handoff.sh, warn-claimed-handoff.sh, block-handoff-placeholder.sh, gate-channel-claim-scope.sh) call tools this story deletes; a claude-config PR deletes them and drops the handoff read from the INBOX block of hooks/session-start.sh, and merges before this release deploys (definition_of_done). Release 8 does not move them: US-52.50's inventory records them retired, already deleted.

e2e: the scenario is release 3's e2e/test/two_sessions_one_repo_test.exs (US-52.20); its checkpoint and move refusals are US-52.45's steps, so this story only removes the channel-claim steps the deletion makes dead.
non_goals: Advisory file soft-locks (channel_lock): kept; release 4 moved them to channel_locks.
Moving claude-config's remaining factory half: release 8; only the callers of deleted tools change here.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.49.3: the migration runs inside loopctl's own database during the deploy migration; a client cut off during the deploy finds the tools gone on reconnect and the work as stories.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.49.1: after the migration every open piece of work lives as a story; no table or keyed post holds a second copy.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.49.3: migrated_from makes a re-run a no-op, so a migration retried after a failed deploy creates nothing twice.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.49.3: the dry run reports the row counts first; the open set is bounded by the 30-day post retention, so the migration is a few hundred rows.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.49.4: after the drop a session reaches an item only through its claim and its holder credential; AC-52.49.7 keeps the release-3 two-sessions scenario passing without channel claims.

defaults: Epic for migrated handoffs without an intake target: 'Migrated handoffs', one per project.
Migrated stories start at stage detected.
A claim whose holder has ended is not carried; its story stays unclaimed for the loop.
definition_of_done: On production after deploy: SELECT to_regclass('channel_claims') is null; SELECT count(*) FROM stories WHERE metadata ? 'migrated_from' equals the dry run's count.
claude-config's PR removing the handoff skill and claim-reading hooks is merged before the deploy, and a fleet session's SessionStart shows no handoff block.
